subject: Next steps — VPC residency & air-gap eligibility for HeathGen (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@heathgen.com>, Marco Silva <m.silva@heathgen.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + immediate asks (VPC residency / air-gap eligibility)

Thanks Sofia and Marco — good to meet you both today. Quick recap from our discovery and the items we agreed to follow up on. Notes below are intentionally concise so we can align next steps.

High-level customer goals and constraints
- Residency & regulatory: PHI must remain in US-only GovCloud regions; no model weights or logs may be exported outside the controlled environment.
- Isolation requirement: customer procurement is prioritizing either an air-gapped on-prem hosting option or a VPC-deployed Private control plane with strictly white-listed egress.
- Key management: KMS with HSM-backed keys required, integration with customer-managed KMS preferred.
- Audit & evidence: SOC2 artifacts, audit log export, and packet-level egress proof for procurement.
- Timeline: procurement evaluating proposals this month; target decision window ~end of June.

Technical constraints called out on the call
- Network: only outbound connectivity allowed from application subnet to specific Redwood endpoints (we agreed to provide exact port/IP list).
- No public-facing NAT that permits unrestricted egress; GovCloud endpoints only.
- Data flow: telemetry and non-PHI metrics must be optional; default should not send identifying metadata.

Action items (owner / ETA)
1) Ben: Share SOC2 excerpt + a minimal VPC port/endpoint list by EOD tomorrow (attaching network-constraints-sheet.xlsx).
2) Karthik: Schedule a deep technical dive to validate HSM/KMS handshake and any kernel-level requirements (suggest Wed 6/20).
3) Laura/Marissa: Draft an initial SOW and ballpark price for a 4-week PoC (private deployment in GovCloud) — deliverable by 6/18.
4) Sofia/Procurement: Confirm procurement timeline and any additional contract requirements (e.g., data processing addendum).

Attachments (stubs): network-constraints-sheet.xlsx — contains initial checklist for ports, subnets, and control-plane DNS we discussed.

If anything below is incorrect or missing, flag and I will update. Otherwise I’ll push SOC2 excerpt + port list by tomorrow.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

--
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@heathgen.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marco Silva <m.silva@heathgen.com>
Cc: procurement <procurement@heathgen.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 17:15:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + immediate asks (VPC residency / air-gap eligibility)

Thanks Ben — that summary looks right. A couple clarifications from procurement and security:

1) Procurement timeline: we aim to have vendor shortlist by 6/25, final selection by 7/02. Can you confirm whether Redwood can sign a FedRAMP-like attestation? If not, we need mitigations listed.

2) Security asks: please include the specific SOC2 sections (CC6, CC7) that map to audit logs and key management. A redacted SOC2 is fine.

3) Network specifics: we need the promised port/ip list and a plain-English description of the control plane endpoints that require egress — we cannot present a blob of FQDNs to our network team.

4) Cost: procurement wants a ballpark for a dedicated 8-GPU pool in GovCloud and a 4-week PoC price (inclusive of support). This can be a range.

We attached a short PDF with our residency acceptance criteria (HeathGen-residency-constraints.pdf) for reference.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Marco and I will circulate any additional procurement docs after the internal review tomorrow.

--
Sofia Ramos
Head of Cloud Security, HeathGen
sofia.ramos@heathgen.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + immediate asks (VPC residency / air-gap eligibility) — docs and port list

Sofia — attaching the requested artifacts. See brief notes below and the attached stubs: SOC2-excerpt.pdf (redacted), vpc-port-list.txt, and a draft SOW outline (SOW-draft-v0.1.docx).

Short answers to procurement/security asks:
- FedRAMP: Redwood does not currently hold a FedRAMP authorization. For GovCloud deployments we provide compensating controls and can surface a remediation/attestation plan. We will document mitigations and put them in the SOW.
- SOC2 sections: SOC2 excerpt highlights controls for logging/audit (CC6) and key management (CC7). See the attached PDF with page references.
- Egress endpoints: vpc-port-list.txt contains an ordered list and plain-English mapping (Control plane API: IPs A.B.C.D/32 + port 443; telemetry optional to telemetry.redwood.com:443). If HeathGen requires IP-only allow-lists we can provide static IPs for the control-plane pool.

Preliminary pricing (ballpark)
- 8-GPU dedicated GovCloud pool: $85k–$120k/month depending on committed throughput and SLA.
- 4-week PoC (private deployment, engineering support, runbook + onboarding): ~$45k–$60k (one-time).

Proposed next steps
1) Karthik — propose two slot options for technical deep dive (60–90m) next week where we validate KMS/HSM handshake and egress-only model.
2) Laura/Marissa — do a SOW price review and add procurement language for attestation options.
3) Sofia/Procurement — confirm whether procurement needs a formal security questionnaire or if the SOC2 excerpt + technical deep dive suffice.

Attachments: SOC2-excerpt.pdf (redacted), vpc-port-list.txt (plain text), SOW-draft-v0.1.docx (outline).

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 16 Jun 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: HeathGen follow-up — owners and timeline

Looping internal owners together so we hit the procurement window. Quick items I captured after Ben's artifacts: 

1) SOW & commercial: Marissa, please convert Ben's draft into a SOW v0.2 with a clear PoC deliverable list and two pricing options (PoC only; PoC + 3mo reserved). Target: 6/18 COB.

2) Legal & procurement language: Ben, I will draft the data processing addendum and mitigation bullet points for FedRAMP gaps. Marissa, include an explicit KMS/HSM integration clause that allows a third-party audit.

3) Technical deep dive: Karthik — please propose two 60–90 minute slots for 6/20 or 6/21. We need to confirm exact port/IP mappings and validate KMS handshake flow.

4) Demo environment: I want a set of sanitized prompts and a short runbook for PoC that proves no PHI leaves the environment. Marissa, can you prepare the PoC checklist?

5) Outreach to procurement: Ben, send a short note to procurement@heathgen.com introducing the SOW timeline and attach the SOC2 excerpt / port list. I can join that thread if needed.

Targets and dates:
- 6/18: SOW v0.2 and ballpark commercial to procurement.
- 6/20–6/21: Technical deep dive with Karthik and HeathGen technical owners.
- 6/25: Vendor shortlist (customer goal).

Link to internal planning doc: https://drive.redwood.com/HeathGen/SCOPEDOC-3241
